items.current: All-India CPI inflation averaged roughly 2-3% in FY 2025-26 (monthly prints near record lows in late 2025). The "desi inflation 10%+" part is the author's own estimate, not an official figure.
items.quote: Government inflation is 6%. But Desi inflation (School fees, Medical, Milk) is 10%+.
items.why: Quotes retail inflation (CPI) as 6%. Headline CPI ran far below that through FY 2025-26.

items.current: EPF interest on employee contributions above Rs 2.5 lakh a year (Rs 5 lakh where there is no employer contribution) is taxable since FY 2021-22. PPF interest is fully exempt.
items.quote: 🚫 Avoid "Lifestyle Inflation". ✅ Buy Term Insurance (Before it gets expensive). ✅ Maximize EPF/PPF (Tax free growth).
items.why: "Tax free growth" is true for PPF but not unconditionally for EPF.

items.current: SGBs are RBI-issued government securities. "Digital gold" sold by apps is not an SGB and is not regulated by SEBI or RBI (SEBI cautioned investors in Nov 2025).
items.quote: Making charges (20%) eat your profit. SGB (Digital Gold) is an asset. Jewelry is fashion.
items.why: Equates Sovereign Gold Bonds with "Digital Gold". They are different products.

items.current: Credit-card revolving interest is typically 36-48% a year depending on the issuer; check the card's own most-important-terms document.
items.quote: Paying only the minimum due on Credit Cards. Interest is 42% per year.
items.why: Single figure stated as fact.

items.current: Making charges vary (roughly 5-25%). GST: 3% on gold value, 5% on making charges (as applicable in FY 2025-26).
items.quote:
👑 Investment vs Ornament Jewelry: You pay 20% Making Charges + 3% GST. Resale value is lower. This is Consumption, not Investment.
Digital Gold / ETF: Pure price exposure. Efficient.
items.why: Making charges are shown as a fixed 20%; GST on the making charge is 5%, on the gold value 3%.

items.current: The government has not opened new SGB tranches since the Feb 2024 series; today they can only be bought on the exchange (often at a premium, thin liquidity). The maturity tax exemption applies to redemption at maturity by the original investor; selling on the exchange is taxed as a capital gain. "Mathematically the best" is an opinion.
items.quote: The only asset in the world that gives you Gold Price Appreciation + 2.5% Interest.
items.why: Presents SGB as something you can buy today and as "the best way to own gold". New SGB tranches have not been issued since early 2024.

items.current: Gold ETFs are SEBI-regulated; app-based "digital gold" is not (SEBI warning, Nov 2025).
items.quote:
👑 Investment vs Ornament Jewelry: You pay 20% Making Charges + 3% GST. Resale value is lower. This is Consumption, not Investment.
Digital Gold / ETF: Pure price exposure. Efficient.
items.why: Groups unregulated digital gold with gold ETFs.

items.current: Savings accounts pay about 2.5-3%. FD rates for general customers are mostly about 6-7% and the 10-year G-Sec yield has been around 6.3-6.7%, not 7.2-7.5%. Check live rates.
items.quote:
🏦 The Indian Reality Most Indians keep money in Savings Accounts (3%) or FDs (6.5%).
The Hack: Government Bonds (G-Secs) often pay 7.2% - 7.5% with higher safety than a private bank FD. Why let the bank keep the spread?
items.why: Rates are a snapshot that is out of date after the RBI repo cuts of 2025.

items.current: Illustrative only; returns depend on the rate cycle and can be negative. Debt-fund gains are taxed at slab rate (no indexation, no LTCG benefit) for units bought after 1 Apr 2023.
items.quote:
☠️ GOD MODE: Duration Risk Long Duration Funds (10 Year+ Bonds): These are highly sensitive to interest rates. If RBI cuts rates, these funds can give 12-15% returns (Capital Gains). If RBI hikes rates, you lose capital.
Strategy: Stick to Liquid Funds or Target Maturity Funds for safety.
items.why: Quotes a return range (12-15%) as what long-duration funds "can give".

items.current: ASM is an exchange (NSE/BSE) framework agreed with SEBI; inclusion uses several parameters, not one 50% jump, and the margins per stage are set by the exchange and have changed. Check the exchange circular.
items.quote:
☠️ GOD MODE: The 1% Knowledge This is what banks don't teach you.
1. The Free Float Trap
A company has a Market Cap of ₹10,000 Cr. But the Owner (Promoter) holds 90% of shares. Only 10% is available for trading. This is Low Free Float. Operators can easily manipulate the price because there is very
items.why: Attributes the ASM list to SEBI and gives a single trigger and a fixed margin.

items.current: A listed company can also raise money later through a follow-on public offer, rights issue, QIP or preferential allotment.
items.quote: You are buying it from another person (Uncle Sharma) who wants to sell it. The company only gets money once: during the IPO (Initial Public Offering). After that, it's just people exchanging ownership.
items.why: Simplification.

items.current: Nifty 50 ETFs charge roughly 0.03-0.10% a year depending on the fund; verify on the fund's factsheet.
items.quote:
🍱 The ETF Thali An ETF (Exchange Traded Fund) is a pre-set Thali.
- Nifty 50 ETF: You get a spoon of Reliance, a bowl of HDFC, a slice of TCS.
- The Cost: Dirt cheap. (Expense Ratio: 0.05%).
- The Logic: You are betting on India's Economy, not one company's CEO.
items.why: A specific fee quoted for "a Nifty 50 ETF".

items.current: SEBI studies found about 9 in 10 individual F&O traders lost money in FY22-FY25 (91% in FY25, average loss about Rs 1.1 lakh). The 66% figure has no source.
items.quote:
☠️ GOD MODE: Option Selling Retailers BUY options (Lottery tickets). Institutions SELL options (The Casino).
Why? Because 66% of the time, markets are sideways. In sideways markets, Option Buyers lose 100% of their premium due to Theta Decay. Option Sellers keep it.
Verdict: Buying options is playin
items.why: Unsourced statistic, and "option buyers lose 100% of premium" overstates it.

items.current: Option writing needs margin well above the premium collected; one gap move can wipe out many months of premium. SEBI's 2024-25 measures (larger contract size, upfront premium, expiry limits) apply to index options.
items.quote:
☠️ GOD MODE: Option Selling Retailers BUY options (Lottery tickets). Institutions SELL options (The Casino).
Why? Because 66% of the time, markets are sideways. In sideways markets, Option Buyers lose 100% of their premium due to Theta Decay. Option Sellers keep it.
Verdict: Buying options is playin
items.why: Encourages option selling without saying that sellers carry very large (for naked calls, unlimited) losses and need large margins.

items.current: USD/INR traded around Rs 88-90 in late 2025.
items.quote:
USD / INR = 83.50 This means: 1 Dollar = 83.50 Rupees.
- If you think India will do well ➔ You BUY INR (Sell USD).
- If you think USA will raise rates ➔ You BUY USD (Sell INR).
items.why: Spot rate is stale.

items.current: Residents may trade currency derivatives only on recognised Indian exchanges (USD/INR, EUR/INR, GBP/INR, JPY/INR); margin trading on foreign forex platforms is not permitted under FEMA (RBI keeps an alert list). Exchange margins are far below 100x.
items.quote: The Power of 100x
items.why: 100x leverage for an Indian resident is not available on legal venues.

items.current: The BIS triennial survey of April 2025 put FX turnover at about USD 9.6 trillion a day (USD 7.5 trillion in 2022).
items.quote: The largest market on Earth ($6 Trillion/Day). Trading the health of nations.
items.why: Out-of-date global turnover.

items.current: Policy rates are no longer about 0% (Japan) and 5% (USA): Japan has been near 0.5-0.75% and the US Fed funds range was cut to about 3.5-3.75% by Dec 2025.
items.quote:
☠️ GOD MODE: The Carry Trade The Strategy: Borrow money in a country with LOW interest rates (e.g., Japan, 0%). Invest that money in a country with HIGH interest rates (e.g., USA, 5%).
Profit: You pocket the 5% difference for free. This is how hedge funds make billions (until the currency crashes).
items.why: Example interest rates are stale.

items.current: General-category FD rates are mostly about 6-7% after the 2025 repo cuts; the 15% hurdle is a rule of thumb, not a standard.
items.quote:
Desi Logic
FD gives 7%. If a business takes your money and generates only 6%, why invest? Look for 15%+.
items.why: Uses 7% as the FD benchmark.

items.current: Healthy ratios differ by sector (banks and NBFCs are structurally highly leveraged; ROE and P/B norms differ). Treat as starting points, not verdicts.
items.quote: Measures how efficiently the company uses shareholders' money. >15% is excellent. <10% is poor.
items.why: Rule-of-thumb thresholds stated as rules.

items.current: Institutions often benchmark execution against VWAP, but they do not only buy near it.
items.quote:
Wholesale Rate
Big dealers (FIIs) only buy near VWAP. They don't pay Retail MRP.
items.why: Overclaim about institutional behaviour.

items.current: Commonly cited estimates of Indian medical inflation range about 10-14% a year depending on the source; none is an official statistic.
items.quote: In the Indian context, medical inflation is roughly 14%. A single bypass surgery or a 10-day ICU stay can delete years of compounding in a week.
items.why: Single figure presented as fact.

items.current: Traditional endowment plans often return about 4-6% a year; CPI was about 2-3% in FY 2025-26, so "losing money to inflation" is weaker today. The point that insurance and investment should be kept separate still stands.
items.quote: Most Indians buy "Endowment" plans (LIC style) because they "get money back." These plans give ~5% returns. Inflation is 6-7%. You are literally losing money to insure yourself.
items.why: Compares ~5% returns with a stale 6-7% inflation.

items.current: Income multiples of 10-20x plus liabilities are common rules of thumb; the right cover depends on dependants, assets and years to retirement. Use the Life Cover tool for a worked estimate.
items.quote: Cover = (Annual Income × 20) + Total Debt
items.why: A formula given as "The FIN-OS Formula" and "anything less is a vulnerability".

items.current: T-bill and liquid-fund yields were about 5.3-6% in FY 2025-26 after the 2025 repo cuts. "Almost zero risk" holds for T-bills, not for every liquid fund.
items.quote:
❌ Savings Account? 3% Interest. You lose money to inflation.
✅ Money Market?
7% Interest. Almost zero risk. Highly liquid.
items.why: Quotes 7% for the money market.

items.current: Commercial paper has a minimum face value of Rs 5 lakh and is mainly bought by institutions; retail access is through debt/liquid funds.
items.quote: T-Bills (Treasury Bills): You lend to the Govt of India for 91, 182, or 364 days. Risk: ZERO. CP (Commercial Paper): You lend to Reliance/Tata for 3 months. Risk: Low. CD (Certificate of Deposit): You lend to HDFC Bank for 1 year. Risk: Low.
items.why: Suggests an individual can lend to a corporate via commercial paper.

items.current: Arbitrage funds are taxed as equity funds: 20% short-term (held under 12 months) and 12.5% long-term gains above Rs 1.25 lakh a year, not 12.5% from 6 months. They are low-risk, not risk-free, and typically returned about 6-7%. Liquid funds are taxed at slab rate (30% only in the top slab).
items.quote:
☠️ GOD MODE: Arbitrage Funds The Tax Hack: Liquid Funds are taxed at your slab rate (30% for high earners). Arbitrage Funds are taxed as Equity (12.5% after 1 year).
Strategy: Use Arbitrage Funds for parking cash > 6 months. It returns 7-8% risk-free but saves you massive tax compared to FDs.
items.why: Tax and return claims are incomplete.

items.current: S&P SPIVA India shows a high underperformance rate for large-cap active funds over 10 years, but mid/small-cap categories differ a lot and the figure changes every report.
items.quote:
The Harsh Truth (SPIVA Report) Active Fund: Manager tries to beat Nifty. Charges 1-2% fee. Passive Fund: Simply copies Nifty. Charges 0.2% fee.
Fact: 80% of Active Funds FAIL to beat Passive Funds over a 10-year period.
items.why: Presents an SPIVA-style statistic as a general fact.

items.current: The regular-vs-direct expense gap is about 0.5-1.5% depending on the scheme; the rupee gain depends on SIP size, tenure and return. Direct plans have no distributor commission; "scam" is the author's framing.
items.quote:
☠️ GOD MODE: The "Regular Plan" Scam Never buy a "Regular" Mutual Fund from a bank or agent.
Regular Plan: Includes 1% commission to the agent every single year from your wealth.
Direct Plan: Zero commission. That 1% compounds. Over 20 years, a Direct plan gives you ₹30-40 Lakhs MORE on a standard S
items.why: A specific rupee gain is stated without its assumptions.

items.current: Checked: for a 20-year loan at 8-10%, one extra EMI each year closes it in about 16.3-16.9 years. "80% of EMI is interest in year one" is right for roughly 8-9% rates and 20 years.
items.quote: The Fix: Pre-pay 1 extra EMI every year. You will close a 20-year loan in 12 years.
items.why: Arithmetic is wrong: one extra EMI a year does not take a 20-year loan to 12 years.

items.current: The figures match a Rs 5,000 monthly SIP at 12% a year (not guaranteed) running 30 years vs 20 years (about Rs 1.75 crore vs Rs 49 lakh). Equity returns are not assured.
items.quote: Start at 25: You invest ₹18 Lakhs -> You get ₹1.7 Crores. Start at 35: You invest ₹12 Lakhs -> You get ₹48 Lakhs.
items.why: The retirement age and the return are not stated.

items.current: CPI inflation averaged about 2-3% in FY 2025-26. "Nifty 50: 12%" is an assumption, not a promise.
items.quote: ⚠️ While CPI is 6%, your Lifestyle costs are growing at 10-12%.
items.why: Uses 6-7% as current inflation.
